text:
incident-bot: SEV2 ALERT - velaris-private-vpc - elevated 5xx rate observed for tenant-dedicated-pool-velaris-1 across ingress ALB (alb-velaris-1) and egress NLB (nlb-egress-velaris). Pager: alice
alice: i'm on it, seeing ~18% 5xx on /api/v1/generate for the last 4m. paging network oncall
bob: @alice oncall-net here. can you paste the target NLB arn and any error codes you see? I'm looking at flow logs
carol: grabbing relevant nginx access logs from the dedicated pool. lots of backend 502/504, but also some connection resets.
alice: nlb arn: arn:aws:elasticloadbalancing:us-west-2:123456789012:loadbalancer/net/nlb-egress-velaris/abcd1234
alice: sample proxy log: \"upstream prematurely closed connection while reading response header from upstream\" - multiple backend targets unhealthy
dave: quick check: route table for private subnet velaris-prod-priv-rtb shows default route to TGW via tgw-02. any recent route changes? I don't see updates in last 24h
bob: flow logs show asymmetric src/dst for 10.10.20.0/24 -> 54.12.34.56 during the spike, return traffic hitting a different subnet's NACL. possible sg/route asymmetry
carol: running target health:
```
aws elbv2 describe-target-health --target-group-arn arn:aws:elasticloadbalancing:...:targetgroup/tg-velaris/5678
# many targets showing \"unhealthy - timeout\"
```
alice: checking DNS — customer uses private Route53 zone velaris.private. ALB CNAME points to internal-alb-123.us-west-2.elb.amazonaws.com TTL=60
eve-csm: Velaris engineering on call just DM'd: \"we're seeing 502s globally for customers in EU/US, can you confirm scope?\" They're asking for ETA for mitigation
alice: scope: only their dedicated-pool (tenant isolation holding), but traffic from their LB -> egress NLB is failing, so user requests erroring; no cross-tenant data observed. telling them containment verified
oncall-net: joining. reading up: suspecting security-group rule preventing ephemeral return ports from NLB when traffic is SNATed by egress proxy. which egress proxy version? is there an inline NAT? 
carol: yes, egress proxy version 2.3.1 in that env. I see SYN packets hitting NLB but RSTs from backend. full packet capture attached to thread (pasted lower)
packetbot: pcap snippet:
```
10:23:45.123 IP 10.10.20.34.52344 > 54.12.34.56.80: S
10:23:45.124 IP 54.12.34.56.80 > 10.10.20.34.52344: R
```
bob: RST from 54.12.34.56 (an intermediate egress instance) suggests SG dropped ephemeral return traffic or the NLB health check target routing changed
alice: immediate mitigation options: 1) add temporary SG rule allowing ephemeral range 1024-65535 from nlb-subnet-cidr, 2) shift Route53 weight to standby NLB (nlb-egress-velaris-b) 3) enable connection drain on ALB and failover
dave: I'm ok applying SG rule for 30m as emergency. will coordinate with security.
carol: opsbot, run playbook: add-sg-rule --sg-id sg-velaris-egress --port-range 1024-65535 --src nlb-subnet-cidr --expires 30m
opsbot: OK queued: change-request CR-8247 created, applying temporarily in 30s
opsbot: applied sg-velaris-egress + ephemeral ports open to nlb subnets, rule expires in 30m (automated revert scheduled)
alice: traffic dropping to 2% 5xx after SG change. good signal. continue monitoring
eve-csm: telling Velaris: \"we've applied temporary network rule, traffic should be improved; we're monitoring and will keep you updated.\" asking for CORS endpoints affected list
carol: still seeing occasional 502s from a subset of targets -- draining target group tg-velaris-2 shows a behind-the-scenes instance with kernel netfilter weirdness. marking it OUT_OF_SERVICE
bob: recommend we shift weighted DNS immediately to secondary NLB so customer requests route to healthy edge while we investigate instance-level root cause
alice: agreed. carol, can you perform weighted shift? update Route53 velaris.private record set to 90% nlb-b / 10% nlb-a for 10m then monitor
carol: executing:
```
aws route53 change-resource-record-sets --hosted-zone-id Z3VELARIS --change-batch '{"Changes":[{"Action":"UPSERT","ResourceRecordSet":{"Name":"api.velaris.private.","Type":"A","SetIdentifier":"nlb-b","Weight":90,"TTL":20,"ResourceRecords":[{"Value":"10.20.30.40"}]}}]}'
```
carol: change submitted, TTL low so propagation quick
alice: metrics: 90% -> 3% 5xx across the board after shift. OK. next: identify root cause on original NLB targets. carol, can you snapshot instance and check kernel msg / conntrack
carol: instance i-0a1b2c3d shows conntrack table saturation during spike; many TIME_WAIT entries and some conntrack failures in dmesg. probable conntrack exhaustion causing established connections to be dropped -> 502
dave: that matches asymmetric flows + SNAT behavior. we should harden conntrack: increase nf_conntrack_max on fleet and add monitor alert. also consider adding eBPF offload in future
bob: action items: (A) scale egress proxy fleet temporarily to absorb new connections (B) increase conntrack on image and rollout (C) keep SG temporary rule until runbook complete
alice: i'm handing incident to network oncall for next 90m to lead remediation and followups. @oncall-net takes lead now
oncall-net: acknowledged. will own escalation to network-eng, set follow-up ticket NET-1192 for conntrack tuning + egress proxy autoscale policy. Marking incident as in mitigation, customer impact reducing
eve-csm: Velaris PM asks for postmortem and ETA for permanent fix — told them we'll provide mitigation timeline within 4 hours and postmortem in 48h
opsbot: deploy-bot: rolling update of egress-proxy v2.4.0 (conntrack improvements) queued to canary 1/5
carol: starting canary deploy to one AZ now, will monitor connections/5xx
alice: thanks team. I'll prepare an incident summary for SRE rotation and include timeline + mitigations. handing off to dave for post-incident action tracking
dave: creating follow-up: NET-1192 (conntrack tuning), OPS-4532 (add permanent SG allowances for NLB to avoid asymmetric failures), CS-784 (customer comms + postmortem)
alice: last check: last_message_ts 2313457030, closing out Slack thread for active paging. if anything regresses, reopen and ping paging list.
incident-bot: Incident updated: status=mitigated severity=sev2 effected_tenants=[velaris] start_ts=2313456789 mitigated_ts=2313457030
